title: Flowering Plant Families
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Flowering Plant Families scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: A rooted branching tree visibly shows the stated sister taxa and their clade relationships.
Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary to encode the supplied evolutionary distances.
The named taxa are legible at the tree tips.
The named clade is visibly highlighted distinctly from the rest of the tree.
A visible scale or distance label identifies the evolutionary-distance interpretation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/rectangular exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly presents a complete rectangular phylogram matching the supplied Newick topology, with variable horizontal branch lengths, legible tip labels, a distinct green Rosids highlight, and a substitutions/site scale.

items.evidence: Fabaceae and Rosaceae are visibly paired as sister taxa, Asteraceae and Lamiaceae form the other sister pair, and both pairs join at the rooted split.
Horizontal branches visibly differ in length, including the unequal terminal branches within both sister pairs.
Fabaceae, Rosaceae, Asteraceae, and Lamiaceae are all clearly legible beside their respective tips.
The Fabaceae–Rosaceae branches are green and the corresponding taxa are enclosed in a pale-green region with a green bracket labeled Rosids.
A visible scale bar is labeled 0.05 substitutions/site, with supporting text identifying horizontal distance as substitutions/site.
